Income tax › Deductions › 80DD

Section 80DD: dependant with a disability

A resident who supports a dependant with a disability can deduct a flat ₹75,000, or ₹1.25 lakh for a severe disability, in the old regime.

Who can claim it

Resident individuals and HUFs who look after a dependent spouse, child, parent, brother or sister with a disability.

The rules for tax year 2026-27 (Income-tax Act, 2025)

  • Flat ₹75,000 (40% or more disability) or ₹1.25 lakh (80% or more), whatever is spent on treatment, training and care, or paid into an approved insurance scheme for the dependant.
  • Not allowed if the dependant claims 80U themselves.
  • A medical certificate is needed.
  • Not allowed in the new regime.

Common questions

Can both 80U and 80DD be claimed for the same person?

No. If the person with the disability claims 80U, nobody can claim 80DD for them.
